newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTS-Australia July-Sept budget deficit A$5.86 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTS-Australia July-Sept budget deficit A$5.86 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit for the first three months of fiscal 1996/97 was A$5.86 billion, compared with A$5.53 billion a year earlier, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Friday.
The headline balance was A$2.25 billion, compared with A$2.57 billion a year earlier, Fahey said in a statement.
The underlying measure excludes the proceeds from asset sales and state government debt repayments.
Outlays for July-September were A$30.66 billion, 1.0 percent below A$30.98 billion in 1995/96 and compared with budgeted growth for 1996/97 of 2.4 percent.
Revenues were A$28.41 billion, compared with A$28.41 billion also a year earlier, and against budgeted growth of 7.0 percent for 1996/97.
Fahey said the fall in outlays reflected a decline in state debt repayments and the receipt of funds in 1995/96 from the sale of the Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd.
The monthly figures are highly volatile and cannot be extrapolated to estimate a final outcome for 1996/97.
